title: Collective Mining Discovers High-Grade Tungsten and Gold Mineralization in Schist at Depth Outside the Apollo Breccia Body
summary: Miami, Florida, September 24, 2026 – Collective Mining Ltd. (NASDAQ: CNL; TSX: CNL) (“Collective” or the “Company”) is...
body_markdown:
- **New high-grade tungsten-gold discovery outside the Apollo Mineral Resource block model: APC150-D4 intersected 8.15 meters grading 14.82 g/t AuEq (0.40% WO3, 8.47 g/t Au, 4 g/t Ag) south of and outside the Apollo breccia body, marking the Company’s first tungsten intersection in surrounding schist in this area.**


- **The discovery lies approximately 680 meters vertically below the base of the shallow tungsten zone represented in the block model for Apollo, with only very limited drilling in this schist unit. Follow-up drilling is planned to test the extent and continuity of this newly identified style of mineralization.**


- **Thirteen new high-grade veins have been discovered, including 1.15 meters grading 57.98 g/t AuEq (55.50 g/t Au, 109 g/t Ag, 0.35% Cu) and 1.25 meters grading 28.73 g/t AuEq (28.60 g/t Au, 6 g/t Ag) in APC-171D. Seven veins lie outside the block model; the remaining six occur within its southwestern margin, with assay grades significantly exceeding the estimates for the corresponding model blocks.**


- **Ramp Zone mineralization extended approximately 35 meters westward** **from the current block model for the Ramp Zone along the southern axis of the breccia margin.** **Both holes were terminated short of their planned target depths within the Ramp Zone due to challenging drilling conditions.**


- **Results are pending for seventeen drill holes testing the Ramp Zone with five additional holes in progress. Multiple holes have intersected visually-identified* mineralization, including areas with localized visible gold, at previously undrilled locations around the circumference of the Apollo breccia body. Drilling has also tested** **below the existing block model.** **APC171-D3 intersected visually-identified* Ramp Zone-style mineralization including localized visible gold, approximately 350 meters below the current block model; assays are pending.**


**Miami, Florida, September 24, 2026 – Collective Mining Ltd. (NASDAQ: CNL; TSX: CNL) (“Collective” or the “Company”)** is pleased to announce assay results for four diamond drill holes at its Guayabales Project in Caldas, Colombia. The results highlight continued exploration potential beyond the currently defined Mineral Resource Model (MR) for the Apollo deposit and include a new high-grade tungsten-gold zone hosted in schist rock outside the southern Apollo breccia body margin.


Drill hole APC150-D4 intersected 8.15 meters grading 14.82 g/t AuEq (0.40% WO3, 8.47 g/t Au and 4 g/t Ag), beginning 927 meters below surface. This is the first time the Company has intersected high-grade tungsten mineralization within the schist outside the southern margin of the Apollo breccia and establishes a brand-new target for drilling. This specific unit of schist extends from surface to more than 1,000 meters vertical and is largely untested.


**Ari Sussman, Executive Chairman, commented:** “What excites me most is how much we still have to test at Apollo. The discovery of high-grade tungsten and gold in the schist outside of the southern margin of the breccia opens a new exploration opportunity at Apollo beyond the breccia body. The new high-grade veins and visually-identified mineralization in drill testing extensions of the Ramp Zone in multiple directions give us compelling targets to test for potential growth beyond the current Mineral Resource. Pending assays and follow-up drilling will guide our next phase of exploration, both within the breccia body and outside of it. With our strong treasury, we can pursue these targets aggressively as we work to establish the full extent of Apollo’s mineralization.”


To date, Collective has received assays for **196,500 meters** of diamond drilling across the Guayabales and San Antonio projects, including results for **132** **,500 meters** at the flagship Apollo deposit, which anchors the Guayabales Project.


With **US$93.7 million** in cash (as of June 30, 2026), the Company is fully funded for its planned **2026 program** , which envisions up to **90,000 meters** of drilling. The Company presently has 13 diamond drill rigs operating across the Guayabales Project. Assay results for 96 drill holes are outstanding, including 17 drill holes into the Ramp Zone.


** Visual observations are not a substitute for assay results and should* *not be interpreted as indicative of grade.*


**Drill Results and Geological Context (See Table 1 and Figures 1-6)**


**New Tungsten Enriched Zone in Schist Outside the Apollo Breccia Body**


APC150-D4, drilled from Pad34, was designed to test the southern margin of the Ramp Zone. Although challenging ground conditions prevented the hole from reaching its planned target depth, it inadvertently intersected a new style of high-grade tungsten and gold rich vein mineralization hosted in schist south of and outside the Apollo breccia body. The principal interval returned 8.15 meters grading 14.82 g/t AuEq (0.40% WO3, 8.47 g/t Au and 4 g/t Ag) from 927 meters below surface, at an elevation of 1,130 meters above sea level (“masl”).


**The intersection lies approximately 680 meters vertically below the base of the shallow tungsten zone represented in the Apollo block model, identifying a new setting for tungsten mineralization in the surrounding schist.** A separate 1.05-meter vein intersected further downhole returned 13.58 g/t AuEq from 943 meters below surface. These results **identify a new exploration target for tungsten-gold-silver veins beyond the Apollo breccia body. Near-term follow-up drilling is planned to test the extent and continuity of this mineralization as there is no drilling between this depth and the near surface, shallow tungsten zone.**


**Thirteen New High-Grade Veins Discovered Within and Beyond the Apollo Block Model**


Mother hole APC-171D was drilled from Pad24 to provide a platform for directional drilling east of the Apollo block model, reaching a downhole depth of more than 1,120 meters. Two directional daughter holes, APC171-D1 and APC171-D2, were subsequently drilled from different points along the mother hole. **Together, the three holes intersected previously unrecognized high-grade veins within and beyond the Apollo block model. Selected results include:** ****

The results demonstrate that high-grade vein mineralization extends beyond **the current Apollo block model and identify additional veins at higher grades within its margins, providing targets for follow-up drilling.**


**Ramp Zone Step Outs Westward Along the Southern Breccia Axis**


After intersecting multiple high-grade veins, holes APC171-D1 and APC171-D2, were extended deeper to test the westward projection of the Ramp Zone along the southern margin of the Apollo breccia body, beyond the western edge of the current block model for the Ramp Zone. Both holes were terminated short of their planned target depths due to difficult ground conditions. Nevertheless, both intersected modest Ramp-style mineralization associated with minor albite, muscovite and epidote alteration, and anomalous bismuth and tellurium. These intersections extend known mineralization approximately 35 meters westward along the southern margin of the Apollo breccia body beyond the current block model for the Ramp Zone.


**Drill motor capacity was subsequently upgraded, materially improving drilling performance from Pad24 and enabling subsequent holes to reach greater depths.** Assay results **are expected in the near term for APC171-D3 and APC171-D4, both of which intersected visually identified Ramp Zone style mineralization with localized visible gold** . APC171-D3 intersected **such material** approximately 350 meters below the current block model. **Visual observations are not a substitute for assay results and do not establish grade.**


Assay results in the Ramp Zone portion of holes APC171-D1 and APC171-D2 are as follows:


**APC171-D1**


- **2.60 m @ 5.35 g/t AuEq from 1,221 m below surface**
- **13.85 m @ 2.30 g/t AuEq from 1,277 m below surface**
- **8.60 m @ 2.71 g/t AuEq from 1,296 m below surface**
- **1.00 m @ 6.60 g/t AuEq from 1,332 m below surface**


**APC171-D2**


- **2.10 m @ 9.21 g/t AuEq from 1,343 m below surface**
- **2.75 m @ 2.60 g/t AuEq from 1,355 m below surface.**


APC171-D2 ended in mineralization as it entered the Company’s projection of the high-grade Ramp Zone, before the target could be fully tested.


**Ramp Zone: A Key Pillar of High-Grade Growth**


Including previously reported drilling along the southeastern and western margins, approximately 470 meters of the interpreted 1.5-kilometer circumference of the Apollo breccia body at depth has now been tested for Ramp Zone mineralization. By comparison, only approximately 315 meters of this circumference had sufficient drilling density for inclusion in the maiden Mineral Resource. The reader should be cautioned that the expanded drilling coverage does not, by itself, establish an extension of the Mineral Resource.


Drilling outside the Mineral Resource has encountered visually identified mineralization at multiple locations, including several occurrences with visible gold. Assay results are pending for 17 drill holes. These visual observations do not establish grades or continuity and laboratory assays are required to determine metal content, while further drilling is needed to assess continuity.


The Ramp Zone is interpreted as a younger reduced vein system related to a reduced intrusion-related gold system with similarities, in terms of mineralogy, to the nearby Marmato Deeps deposit, owned by Aris Mining. Located approximately 1.75 kilometers apart, both the Ramp Zone and Marmato Deeps systems commence at broadly similar elevations and host very similar gold-and-silver-bearing sulphide assemblages. At the Ramp Zone, mineralization occurs with pyrite and pyrrhotite, accompanied by minor bismuth, tellurium, and locally arsenopyrite-bearing sulphides, hosted in veinlet stockworks, cracks and miarolitic cavities of the breccia body. Alteration is dominated by albite, actinolite, muscovite and epidote.


A key distinguishing feature of Ramp Zone-style mineralization is the occurrence of high gold grades relative to publicly reported results from Marmato Deeps. The Company attributes this superior grade profile in places primarily to the higher porosity of the host rock: mineralization at the Ramp Zone is emplaced within a porous crackle breccia matrix, which provides greater permeability for metal-bearing fluids compared to the porphyry host rock at Marmato Deeps.


**Cautionary Note to Readers:**


Although Apollo (including the Ramp Zone) and the Marmato Lower Mine (also referred to as the Bulk Mining Zone or formerly as Marmato Deeps) share certain geological characteristics, information regarding the Marmato Lower Mine is not necessarily indicative of mineralization in the Ramp Zone. Information regarding the Marmato Lower Mine has not been independently verified by the Company or its Qualified Person in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”). All information presented herein regarding the Marmato Lower Mine is derived from the NI 43-101 compliant technical report titled “Technical Report for the Marmato Gold Mine, Caldas Department, Colombia, PFS of the Lower Mine Expansion Project,” with an effective date of June 30, 2022 (filed November 23, 2022). This report is available on Aris Mining Corporation’s website at: https://www.aris-mining.com/operations-and-projects/marmato.

Copper and WO3 are included in AuEq where the intercept’s copper grade is 0.04% or higher and WO3 grade is 0.02% or higher. A dash (—) in the copper and WO3 column indicates a grade below 0.04% and 0.02% respectively.


4. Recovery assumptions are based on metallurgical results announced on August 25, 2026 and used in the Maiden Mineral Resource announced on September 8, 2026.

**About Collective Mining Ltd.** ****


Founded by the team that developed and sold Continental Gold Inc. to Zijin Mining for approximately $1.4 billion in enterprise value, Collective is a gold, silver, copper and tungsten exploration company with projects in Caldas, Colombia. The Company’s two projects are located directly within an established mining camp with ten fully permitted and operating mines.


The Company’s flagship project, Guayabales, is anchored by Apollo, a large-scale, bulk-tonnage and high-grade gold-silver-copper-tungsten deposit that hosts a maiden Mineral Resource of 2.58 million ounces AuEq Indicated (37.0 Mt at a grade of 2.17 g/t AuEq) and 2.83 million ounces AuEq Inferred (48.2 Mt at a grade of 1.83 g/t AuEq). The Company’s objectives at the Guayabales Project are to continue expansion and infill drilling at Apollo while advancing technical, environmental and permitting work across the project.


Management, insiders, a strategic investor and close family and friends own 45.2% of the outstanding shares of the Company and, as a result, are fully aligned with shareholders. The Company is listed on both Nasdaq and the TSX under the trading symbol “CNL”.

**Technical Information** ****


Samples were cut by Company personnel at Collective Mining’s core facility in Caldas, Colombia. Diamond drill core was sawed and then sampled in maximum 2-meter intervals, stopping at geological boundaries. Drill hole core diameter is a mix of PQ, HQ and NQ depending on the depth of the drill hole. Core samples have been prepared and analyzed at ALS laboratory facilities in Medellin, Colombia and Lima, Peru for copper, gold and silver assays, and multi-element ICP. ALS is an accredited laboratory which is independent of the Company. Gold assays are obtained by fire assay fusion with AAS finish on a 50g sample (Au-AA24). Any samples returning > 10 g/t were then reanalyzed by fire assay with gravimetric finish on a 50g sample (Au-GRA22). Copper and silver were assayed by inductively coupled plasma – Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) following a 4-acid digestion. Samples were also analyzed for a suite of 48 elements with ME-MS61 plus mercury and a sequential copper leach analysis was completed on each sample with copper greater than 10,000 parts per million. Blanks, duplicates, and certified reference standards are inserted into the sample stream to monitor laboratory performance. Crush rejects and pulps are kept and stored in a secured storage facility for future assay verification. No capping has been applied to sample composites. The Company utilizes a rigorous, industry-standard QA/QC program.


For further information regarding the Apollo Mineral Resource, including the effective date, data verification, key assumptions, parameters and methods used to estimate the Mineral Resource, and related risks, see the Company’s news release dated September 8, 2026 entitled “Collective Mining Announces Maiden Mineral Resource for its Apollo Deposit at the Guayabales Project”.
